anchors.app (folder): I=100% (Ca=0, Ce=19) — leaf, imported by nobody. CORRECT.
anchors.scheduling/core (folder): I=24% (Ca=13, Ce=4) — stable; Ce driven by @shared/lib/result + date-fns in policy.ts.
anchors.shared/lib (folder): I=16% (Ca=27, Ce=5) — stable, heavily depended on. CORRECT.

anchors.note: depcruise Ce includes npm deps, which inflates I for leaf UI SFCs (they import vue/reka-ui). Read at folder granularity. Gradient is correct: core+shared stable (near 0), app maximally unstable (leaf). LEADING INDICATOR: rising instability of slices/*/core folders over time = the architecture inverting; it currently sits at 13-24% (0% for types).

rule7_audit.method: for each src/shared/** module, count DISTINCT importing slices (via depcruise reverse edges)

findings.unused_primitive: shared/lib/useDebounce.ts has ZERO importers — dead/speculative code. Not caught by no-orphans (it imports vue, so depcruise's orphan=no-in-AND-no-out definition does not fire). Rule 7 says a thing needs 3+ same-reason usages to be in shared/; this has zero.
findings.caveat: The single-slice hits are shadcn-vue DESIGN-SYSTEM primitives (Table/Input/Label/Alert). The constitution treats shadcn primitives as legitimately shared regardless of current usage count, which CONFLICTS with Rule 7's '3+ usages' guideline. The Rule-7 meter cannot distinguish 'premature domain promotion' (real smell) from 'design-system primitive not yet widely used' (fine). It needs a shared/ui carve-out, else it false-positives on the whole primitive library. useDebounce (0 uses) is the one unambiguous finding.

churn_by_layer.collection_script: git log --all --format= --name-only | grep -E '^apps/web/src/' | sed -E 's#^apps/web/src/slices/[^/]+/(core|data|ui)/.*#\1#; s#^apps/web/src/shared/.*#shared#; s#^apps/web/src/app/.*#app#; s#^apps/web/src/slices/[^/]+/(index|routes)\..*#slice-root#' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
churn_by_layer.expected_shape_on_real_repo: ui highest, core lowest. On the starter, shared=32 dominates only because the whole shadcn primitive set was created in the initial commit; core=6 is already lowest-tier, which is the correct direction.
churn_by_layer.interpretation: core churn climbing toward ui churn over time = business rules leaking upward or framework leaking down.

cross_slice_pr_rate.definition: fraction of merged PRs whose changed files span 2+ distinct slices (excluding app/ and shared/).
cross_slice_pr_rate.query: for each merged PR: git show --name-only --format= <merge> | grep '^apps/web/src/slices/' | sed -E 's#.*/slices/([^/]+)/.*#\1#' | sort -u | wc -l  ; count PRs where that is >=2, divide by total merged PRs.
cross_slice_pr_rate.baseline_on_starter: N/A (2 commits, no PR history). Meter defined for the real repo.
cross_slice_pr_rate.interpretation: a HIGH cross-slice PR rate means the slice boundaries do not match how the domain actually changes — no enforcement can fix mis-drawn slices; it is a re-slicing signal.

baseline_and_disable_counts.monotonic_invariant: both must only ever decrease; enforced by scripts/check-baseline-size.ts (baseline) and scripts/check-no-disable-comments.ts (disables). At 0/0 the ratchet is at its floor.
baseline_and_disable_counts.publish_location: CI job summary on every run (arch:baseline:check + arch:no-disable), and should be echoed to a tracked METRICS row so trend is visible across PRs.
